notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), and no hardware was attached, imported or run.

WHAT IT SERVES: the card's models[0], assets/xmls/particle/main.xml, as a MujocoDriver in simulated mode R0. cap.world.step.v1 takes {ticks, action: {ctrl: [...]}}; the bridge writes data.ctrl and runs mj_step ticks times. cap.world.reset.v1 restores the model defaults with mj_resetData + mj_forward. The state is the bridge's integration state (time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed), with timestep_ms 5.0 from the model's <option timestep="0.005"/>. The card's second model, assets/xmls/particle_hinge/main.xml, is not served: one package serves one device, and this driver uses models[0].

WHY THIS SHAPE: the card is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, and the upstream is a MuJoCo model repository whose world-generation layer runs on mujoco-py 1.50 (README.md:13, requirements.txt:7); the card's models are MJCF assets. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed where the gate runs (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is this package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py (a module factory, not an upstream simulator class). The lock names it .fake:fake_mujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF text for the two motors, the three slide joints and the option timestep, but integrates a placeholder joint motion proportional to each control value; it resolves no contact, constraint, friction or actuator force model. The fidelity gaps list every difference.

NOT COVERED: MuJoCo itself was never imported, so no trajectory was compared with the real engine; the upstream WorldBuilder, placement/randomization layer, Env wrapper and rendering are not part of this driver; the second card model is not served; no physical device is modelled and nothing was validated against hardware.

LIMITS: the driver declares no numeric limit. The model's two <motor> actuators state gear 100 but no ctrlrange (assets/xmls/particle/main.xml:16-19), so the model bounds no control value and the bridge publishes no action.ctrl limit; no limit was invented and no operator-required path was added. The step input still requires exactly 2 control values, derived from model.nu.

WARNINGS (all expected under PLAYBOOK.md section 8 and the family bridges, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is a stand-in mujoco module rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, the simulator-family inputs; G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE because no actuating capability has a declared limit to probe, so the suite awards CL2 while every other CL3 test passed. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised.

TESTS: test_driver.py keeps mhs.testing.check_driver and adds seven cases (model shape from the MJCF, a step advancing time and the actuated joints, the absent control range, a wrong-length ctrl refused, reset restoring the defaults, the published fidelity contract, and the e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1.
